title: Highest temperature in London on August 9?
description:
This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 9 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the London City Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/gb/london/EGLC.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Latest numerical weather prediction models from Météo-France and the ECMWF point to a peak temperature near 33–34°C in Paris on August 9 under largely sunny skies and light southerly flow, following several days of elevated heat across western Europe. High-pressure dominance has suppressed cloud cover and allowed strong daytime insolation, while the urban heat island effect around central stations adds a degree or two relative to rural baselines. Ensemble spread and minor differences in boundary-layer moisture or afternoon mixing explain why 33°C and 34°C remain the closest outcomes, with 35°C still plausible if the warmest model solutions verify or if the official measurement captures a brief spike. Updated model runs and Météo-France bulletins in the next 12–18 hours will likely narrow the range before the daily maximum is recorded.

eventMetadata.context_description: A strong cold front and associated cut-off low are advancing across the Western Cape on August 9, 2026, drawing in cooler maritime air and increasing cloud cover that limits daytime solar heating. Official guidance from the South African Weather Service and recent model consensus point to a maximum near 13–15 °C in Cape Town, well below the long-term August average of roughly 17 °C, with light showers or drizzle further suppressing temperatures. Light to moderate southerly or south-westerly winds will enhance mixing of the cooler air mass, while the timing of frontal passage keeps the peak heating window short. Traders have therefore concentrated implied probability on 14 °C (57 %) and 13 °C (25.5 %), reflecting the latest forecast shift from warmer conditions observed on August 8. Updated model runs and any SAWS briefing on Sunday morning remain the key near-term catalysts that could refine these odds.

eventMetadata.context_description: Current short-term forecast models from the National Weather Service and private providers converge on a highest temperature near Chicago’s late-summer climatological normal of 83 °F for August 9, with ensemble guidance showing limited spread around 80–84 °F. A weak surface high and modest southwesterly flow are expected to limit daytime heating while boundary-layer moisture and possible scattered clouds temper peak readings, keeping the most likely outcome in the 82–83 °F bin that currently leads trader pricing. Minor model differences in cloud timing or wind speed explain the tight clustering of the next-nearest bins (80–81 °F and 84–85 °F), while probabilities drop sharply outside that narrow range because historical analogs and current guidance indicate little chance of either strong cold advection or a heat burst. Updated model runs and afternoon observations tomorrow will provide the final resolution inputs.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Coastal marine layer effects and onshore flow are the dominant factors capping highs near 78°F for Los Angeles on August 9.** Persistent low-level stratus and patchy dense fog—common in early August along the coast—limit solar heating, with the National Weather Service forecasting gradual clearing after mid-morning and a high near 77°F at representative stations like LAX. This aligns with climatological norms for the period, where marine influence typically holds coastal maxima in the mid-70s to low-80s.

Trader consensus around the 78-79°F bin (51%) versus 76-77°F (27.5%) and 80-81°F (20%) reflects uncertainty in exact fog clearance timing and minor model variations in boundary-layer moisture. Recent observations from August 7–8 show highs of 76–80°F under similar conditions, supporting the tight clustering while downweighting extremes above 82°F. Updated NWS briefings and morning satellite trends on clearing will be the key near-term drivers before resolution.

Shorter-range updates through 8 August have shown little deviation from these values, reinforcing trader consensus around the central tercile of the historical distribution. Any notable shift would require an unexpected clearing trend or stronger subsidence that allows greater insolation, scenarios that remain low-probability given the entrenched moisture pattern.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Zhengzhou Xinzheng International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 9 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Zhengzhou Xinzheng International Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/cn/zhengzhou/ZHCC.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent numerical weather prediction models from agencies including the Met Office and BBC project a maximum of 31–32°C in Zhengzhou on August 9 under typical late-summer high-pressure conditions with light northeasterly flow. This narrow range drives the closely matched market-implied odds near 38% each for 31°C and 32°C or higher, reflecting genuine forecast uncertainty from minor differences in cloud cover, humidity, and boundary-layer mixing that can shift peak readings by 1°C. Historical August averages near 32°C provide context, while updated model runs tomorrow morning represent the next key data point likely to refine trader consensus ahead of official observations.
